claims.text: The predictive approach can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The approach uses machine-learning models trained on alloy compositions and corresponding thermal-conductivity values.
A diverse training dataset enables the proposed predictive performance.
Differences in alloy-composition complexity affect phonon scattering.
Machine-learning models can learn composition–thermal-conductivity patterns from the dataset.
Learning these patterns allows the models to predict thermal conductivity.
The approach will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity alloys more accurately than current predictive approaches.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys having compositions similar to those represented in its training dataset.
Complex phonon-scattering mechanisms create uncertainty in the approach's accuracy.
Limited diversity in the training dataset creates uncertainty in the approach's accuracy.
The approach can be tested by comparing predicted thermal-conductivity values with experimental measurements on a set of high-entropy alloys.
Laser-flash analysis or time-domain thermoreflectance can provide the thermal-conductivity measurements for the benchmark.
The hypothesis is falsified if prediction errors exceed 10% for at least 20% of the tested alloys.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and conditions describe the training dataset as diverse, whereas the uncertainty field attributes uncertainty to the dataset's limited diversity.
